content: These guidelines are part of the interim guidance supplementing the 2016 consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection. 1. Elaine Abrams (ICAP, Columbia University, USA): Participated in pediatric antiretroviral therapy (ART) advisory boards for ViiV (2016, $4,999) and Merck (2015, $3,750). These financial interests were deemed non-significant, and she participated fully in the guideline development process. 2. Florence Anam (ICW Global, Kenya): No conflicts of interest were reported, and she participated fully. 3. Linda Barlow-Mosha (Makerere University-Johns Hopkins University Research Collaboration, Uganda): No conflicts of interest were reported, and she participated fully. 4. Mark Boyd (University of Adelaide, Australia): Served on HIV advisory boards for Gilead (2018, $7,500) and ViiV (current, $15,000). Research grants to his institution included funding from MSD ($228,048, current) and Gilead ($37,500, current; $22,500, 2018). These financial interests were deemed significant, and he was excluded from voting on recommendations for antiretroviral regimens. 5. Alexandra Calmy (Geneva University Hospital, Switzerland): Received unrestricted grants to support the HIV day hospital at Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève. No conflicts of interest were reported, and she participated fully. 6. Mohamed Chakroun (Monastir University Hospital, Tunisia): No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 7. Martin Choo (Kuala Lumpur AIDS Support Services, Malaysia): Participated in a patient advisory board for long-acting HIV ARV cabotegravir ($886). No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 8. Mark Cotton (Stellenbosch University, South Africa): Consultant for ViiV (attended a neurocognitive meeting) and speaker for MSD. These financial interests were deemed non-significant, and he participated fully. 9. Serge Eholié (Treichville University Teaching Hospital, Côte d’Ivoire): No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 10. Tendani Gaolathe (Ministry of Health, Botswana): No conflicts of interest were reported, and she participated fully. 11. Andreas Jahn (ITECH, Malawi): No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 12. Sergii Antoniak (Ukraine Center for Public Health, Ukraine): No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 13. Nagalingeswaran Kumarasamy (YRGCARE Medical Centre, India): No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 14. Thuy Le (Duke University, USA): Co-investigator in a clinical trial comparing raltegravir and efavirenz for first-line treatment of HIV/Hepatitis C co-infection, funded by Merck ($200,000 to the University of Hawaii). Antiretroviral agents were donated by Gilead. These financial interests were deemed non-significant, and she participated fully. 15. Valerianne Leroy (INSERM, ANRS, France): No conflicts of interest were reported, and she participated fully. 16. Othoman Mellouk (ITPC, Morocco): No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 17. Irene Mukui (Ministry of Health, Kenya): No conflicts of interest were reported, and she participated fully. 18. Angela Mushavi (Ministry of Health and Child Care, Zimbabwe): Received support to attend ICASA 2017 and present at an Alere Satellite session ($3,939). These financial interests were deemed non-significant, and she participated fully. 19. Landon Myer (University of Cape Town, South Africa): No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 20. Pablo Rojo (Complutense University of Madrid, Spain): Principal investigator of the ODYSSEY study on dolutegravir in children as second-line therapy, funded by ViiV (€6 million to the PENTA Foundation). These financial interests were deemed non-significant, and he was excluded from voting on recommendations for antiretroviral regimens. 21. Gayle Sherman (University of the Witwatersrand, South Africa): No conflicts of interest were reported, and she participated fully. 22. Francois Venter (University of the Witwatersrand, South Africa): Participated in advisory boards for Tibotec, Mylan, ViiV, and Gilead (>$1,000 each). Speaker honoraria were received from Merck, GSK, Adcock, Aspen, Roche, ViiV, Gilead, and Mylan (<$1,000 each). Principal investigator of the ADVANCE study (funded by Unitaid, USAID, and South African MRC, $5 million). Drugs for the ADVANCE study were donated by ViiV and Gilead. These financial interests were deemed significant, and he was excluded from voting on recommendations for antiretroviral regimens. 23. Eric Goemaere (MSF, South Africa): No conflicts of interest were reported, and he participated fully. 24. Annemarie Wensing (University Medical Center Utrecht, Netherlands): Consultancy fees from ViiV, Gilead, Merck, Janssen, and CLJI (approximately €2,500) were directed to the university. Received unrestricted educational grants from Janssen, ViiV, Gilead, Merck, and CLJI (<€5,000 each). Investigator-initiated research grants to the institution included €300,000 from Janssen and €10,000 from Gilead. These financial interests were deemed non-significant, and she participated fully. 25. Wendy Stevens (University of the Witwatersrand and NHLS, South Africa): Received grants from the MRC for novel TB diagnostics and from the Gates Foundation for innovation. Reagents for diagnostics were provided by Roche, Abbott, and Cepheid. No conflicts of interest were reported, and she participated fully. 26. Thanyawee Puthanakit (Chulalongkorn University, Thailand): Received research grants from ViiV and Gilead ($100,000 each) to the research institution. These financial interests were deemed non-significant, and she participated fully. 27. Tsitsi Apollo (Ministry of Health, Zimbabwe): No conflicts of interest were reported. 28. Martin Auton (Global Fund, Switzerland): No conflicts of interest were reported. 29. Shaffiq Essajee (UNICEF, USA): No conflicts of interest were reported. 30. Ade Fakoya (Global Fund, Switzerland): No conflicts of interest were reported. 31. Marcelo Freitas (ICAP, Mozambique): No conflicts of interest were reported. 32. Beatriz Grinsztejn (Fundação Oswaldo Cruz, Brazil): Received research support from NIH, Brazilian MoH, Brazilian Research Council, ANRS, amfAR, Gilead, and BMS. Less than $10,000 was received from pharmaceutical companies. These financial interests were deemed non-significant. 33. Diane Havlir (University of California, San Francisco, USA): Received research grants from NIH to the institution. No conflicts of interest were reported.
